Nina R: Quick questionI
m a contractor working 60% (3 days/week). There was a local bank holiday that fell during the companyyear-end blackout and my manager told me we couldne staffing it. Can that day be carried over or paid out? cc @People Ops
People Ops: Hi Nina riefly: contractors and part-time folks are handled case-by-case. If the holiday was during a mandatory blackout and you could not reasonably take it, we can either carry it over pro-rata or do a payroll payout. Manager confirmation + HR form required.
Nina R: Thanks orgot which form to use?
People Ops: Use the blackout-exception form here: https://intranet.redwood/hr-forms/blackout-exception. Attach a short manager note and your contract. Policy excerpt pasted below for quick ref.
```
Excerpt: Bank holidays during mandatory blackout windows
- Employees: default carryover to next leave year unless local law requires payout.
- Contractors/Part-time: pro-rated; HR may approve carryover or equivalent payout when leave could not be taken due to business-critical coverage.
- Approvals: manager confirmation + HR sign-off. Payroll deadlines may affect payout timing.
```
Jorge M: I can confirm Nina was scheduled on the client rotation that week. Ian sign the manager confirmation. :+1:
People Ops: Great, thanks Jorge. Please fill the form and select resolution = "carryover" (or "payout" if you prefer). We've opened case HR-2026-4991 for tracking.
Nina R: Is there a deadline? Payroll cutoff is coming up for my contractor payroll.
People Ops: Submit within 30 days of blackout end for standard handling. If you need a payout this cycle, flag the form "urgent" and include payroll cutoff date; we'll try to escalate but cannot guarantee before cutoff.
calendar-bot: Reminder: company blackout window Dec 24 ec 31. https://calendar.redwood/blackouts
Nina R: Submitted the form and uploaded Jorge's note + my contract. Marked urgent. Thank you!
People Ops: Received. We'll validate pro-rate (3/5 = 0.6 day) and update HR-2026-4991. Expect confirmation within 3-7 business days. :white_check_mark:
